series: Climate Fiscal Policy Brief No. 5.3 · October 2026
title: Validating CPAT

slides.title: Validating CPAT: Baselines, Back-Casts and Model Comparisons
slides.subtitle: How far a finance ministry can trust the Climate Policy Assessment Tool
slides.message: CPAT's published checks support it for ranges and for comparing policies, not for point forecasts. Its results turn on the price elasticities, and every check predates the 2026 bug fixes, so the checks should be rerun.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity

slides.title: A carbon-pricing decision rests on a forecast, and CPAT's forecast has a wide error band

slides.text: If the response to the price is off by half, so are the revenue estimate and the gap to the pledge.
slides.source: CPAT methodology (2023), Parameter Sensitivity Analysis; CPAT-AI bug register, release 1.1.0 (2026).

slides.title: Four tests answer four different questions, and passing one says little about the others

points.text: does the model match the data in its starting year? Built in by calibration, so weak evidence.
started in 2000, does it reproduce what happened by 2017? The closest to an out-of-sample test.
do other energy models, and studies of real carbon prices, give similar answers?
does independent code compute the same numbers? Verification, not validation, but a precondition.
the three with other energy models report no measure of fit.

slides.source: Working paper 5.3, Table 1; Sargent (2013); Wilson et al. (2021).

slides.title: Calibration makes the base year right by construction and can carry a data break into every year

points.lead: Emissions are scaled to the inventory.
points.text: For Egypt, by 0.930: the 2021 inventory (211.05 Mt) over the model's 2022 estimate (226.97 Mt).
The calibrated baseline runs 16%, 32% and 29% below the inventory in 2022, 2023 and 2024.
it misses 2023, where a separate fuel-use shock adds to the gap.

points.lead: So compare the baseline with the inventory
points.text: before using it; policy-against-baseline comparisons hide the gap.

slides.source: CPAT-AI model documentation, Emissions (2026); gaps recomputed in working paper 5.3, Section 4.

slides.title: Against other energy models CPAT is of the same order; only power investment timing differs much

points.text: world CO₂, primary energy and power mix of the same order; gaps on oil aggregation, Russia and nuclear.
the response of emissions to carbon prices of $0–120 has about the same slope.

points.lead: World Bank power planning model (EPM), 34 countries:
points.text: similar generation mix at about $40/tCO₂; EPM builds in lumps, CPAT spreads investment.
"same order of magnitude" could mean 5% or 30%.

slides.source: CPAT methodology (2023), Model comparisons and Appendix H; working paper 5.3, Sections 4 and 6.
